editorial.headline: Light Construction Metalwork, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25111 covers non-aluminium structural metal products for light construction, open across all business scales and nationally available to full foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25111 is the manufacturing lane for non-aluminium structural metal products used in light construction. In plain English, it covers the making of iron fences, grilles, doors, windows, vents, stairs, and similar light-construction metal goods. The emphasis is on fabricated structural products that belong to ordinary building work, not heavy structural steel or specialised pressure equipment.

That makes the code practical for operators whose business is fabrication rather than installation advice, retail trading, or general contracting. A workshop producing metal doors, stair elements, window frames, ventilation pieces, or security grilles would read naturally within the scope described in the record. The activity is also not confined to one business size: the record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the same classification can describe a small fabrication shop or a larger manufacturing operation, provided the activity remains within the stated light-construction product scope.

The national investment position is straightforward. According to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, the record classifies the activity as TERBUKA and sets pma_max_asing at 100. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national ceiling should be read as 100% foreign ownership. There is no partial cap in the slim record, and no additional national threshold, licence, tax, timeline, or minimum-capital condition is stated here, so none should be added to the interpretation.

The Bali picture is also unusually clean. The record does not block this activity for PMA registration in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the provincial moratorium. The moratorium itself is still important context: the record says Bali blocks all Low plus Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But this activity, on the record provided, sits outside that block. The honest conclusion is therefore simple: nationally, KBLI 25111 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the record does not mark it as blocked.
